outcome: Maternal outcomes (labor duration, episiotomy rates, maternal complications)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, head circumference, NICU admissions, neonatal complications)
cohort: The study analyzed 65 women who underwent vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery, divided into primigravid and multigravid groups.
finding: Primigravid women experienced significantly longer labors and higher episiotomy rates, while multigravid women delivered neonates with higher birth weights and larger head circumferences, though overall neonatal and maternal complication rates did not significantly differ by parity.
mod_finding: Parity influences specific outcomes of vacuum-assisted vaginal deliveries, with vacuum assistance potentially preventing asphyxia by expediting labor.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was measured, with multigravid women delivering neonates with higher birth weights; specific inclusion criteria based on weight were not mentioned.
